anomalies.observed: Each fan-tach input has a plain diode inserted in series between the fan-tach node and the MCU pull-up/GPIO node: D2 anode (pin 1) sits on Net-(D2-A) (with R1 pull-up and U4 pin 31 / GPIO21), D2 cathode (pin 3) sits on NET0006 with the fan header J5.3 and the TVS D10; identically D11 anode on Net-(D11-A) (R2 pull-up, U4 pin 30 / GPIO20) and D11 cathode on NET0010 with J10.3 and TVS D8.
anomalies.expected: The spec describes the fan-tach inputs as TVS-diode-protected inputs (only D_TVS on the fan-tach lines; 'Monitors 2 fan tachometers (NUM_FANS = 2) with TVS-diode-protected inputs'). The pull-up and MCU sense pin should therefore sit on the same node as the fan-tach signal and its TVS clamp, with no series diode in the sense path.

evidence.quote: Monitors 2 fan tachometers (NUM_FANS = 2) with TVS-diode-protected inputs, and raises a run fault if a fan stalls.
the D_TVS symbols in the design, D5/D6, are used elsewhere — see Thermocouple/fan section

anomalies.impact: The MCU no longer senses the fan-tach node directly; it senses the anode of a forward-biased diode whose cathode is pulled to the fan's open-collector low. When the fan pulls low, the sense node sits at one diode drop above the fan's saturation voltage (roughly 0.6-0.8 V), which is at/above the ESP32-C3 V_IL (~0.25*3.3 V), so a stalled/low tach may read as logic high and the fan-stall fault may not be detected reliably. The TVS clamp also now protects only the fan-side node, not the MCU-side node.

anomalies.observed: A 2-pin screw terminal J11 is placed with pin 1 on GND and pin 2 tied directly to the heater-control net /Microcontroller/NET0005, which also carries ESP32 GPIO1 (U4.13), the high-side switch IN/DIAG_EN (U9.1/U9.2) and the heater indicator LED D1.
anomalies.expected: The heater-control net is an internal logic signal (GPIO1 driving the TPS1H200 inputs). The spec's connector list contains no screw terminal on this signal; the intended external connectors are the barrel jack, USB-C, thermocouple terminals, fan headers and the heater output terminal.

evidence.quote: IN/DIAG_EN (pins 1/2) are both driven from ESP32 GPIO1 (net /Microcontroller/HEATER)

anomalies.impact: Exposes the ESP32 GPIO1 / high-side-switch input node to an external terminal block. Any external short or load applied at J11 would load/overdrive the GPIO1 output and the TPS1H200 IN/DIAG_EN inputs, altering or defeating heater control.
